newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oil monopoly to freeze overseas investment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oil monopoly to freeze overseas investment.

text.p: Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Thursday it would halt new overseas investments temporarily in response to the economics ministry's call to strengthen local investments.

"Chinese Petroleum has decided to halt all overseas investment projects to respond to the economics ministry's latest call to strengthen domestic investments," company spokeswoman Ho Li-chun told Reuters by telephone.
All overseas investment projects still in the initial contact phase would be halted temporarily, it said.
The company also will freeze projects that are listed on the firm's stalled 1996/97 (July/June) budget, which has yet to be approved by parliament, Ho said.
"Once parliament passes the budget, we will immediately continue those investments, but the investments may be hurt because of the delay," she said.
Contracted projects would continue as planned.
"We will continue all the overseas projects that we have already signed contracts with," Ho said.
Many of the contracted projects were included in the previous year's budget and have parliamentary approval.
Among the projects being halted are a petrochemical zone development project in Malaysia and an oil refinery plant in Brunei, Ho said.
Some projects in Vietnam and Indonesia also will be halted, She said.
